final.from: The source describes it exactly this way: changes in the stock price affect the hedge asymmetrically, and the gain or loss on the short stock position tends to exceed the corresponding loss or gain on the convertible bond.
final.to: The source describes the effect as an asymmetry: changes in the stock price affect the hedge asymmetrically. When the stock falls, the gain on the short stock exceeds the loss on the convertible; when it rises, the gain on the convertible exceeds the loss on the short stock. (Stowell's own sentence, that the gain or loss on the short stock tends to exceed the corresponding loss or gain on the convertible, holds only for a falling stock. Recognise that wording if it appears in an exam option, but the mechanism is that the convex leg wins in both directions.)
